texts.preamble: Nitesh Kumar Bajania @ Nilesh Kumar ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 26 August, 2021 Author: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi Bench: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi 1 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi W.P.(Cr.) No. 9 of 2019
texts.facts: This petition has been heard through Video Conferencing in view of the guidelines of the High Court taking into account the situation arising due to COVID-19 pandemic. None of the parties have complained about any technical snag of audio-video and with their consent these matters have been heard. This petition has been filed challenging order dated 25.09.2018 passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhanbad in connection with Food Safety Case No. 03/2016 whereby penalty of Rs. 50,000/- has been imposed upon the petitioner for violation of Section 51 of the Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006.
texts.arguments: Mr. Indrajit Sinha, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that at the time of filing of this criminal writ petition, Tribunal was not functioning under that Act and subsequent thereto Tribunal has been constituted in the year, 2019. Since, the Tribunal has been constituted, this Court feels that it would be appropriate for the Nitesh Kumar Bajania @ Nilesh Kumar ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 26 August, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86047554/ 1 petitioner to challenge the impugned order before the Tribunal. Accordingly, petitioner is directed to approach the Tribunal by way of filing appropriate appeal. If such appeal is filed within a period of three weeks from today, the Tribunal shall consider the pendency of this petition before this Court. Till filing of appeal within three weeks, no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioner with regard to order dated 25.09.2018 passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhanbad in connection with Food Safety Case No. 03/2016.
